units.title: OP Stack chains with a non-ETH gas token
angles: Arithmetic and control flow. Read the interpreter this network runs at the release its endpoint reports, and any compiler, bytecode rewriting, caching or code analysis stage in front of it. Cover the 256 bit integer library and its pinned version, MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, the comparisons, JUMP and JUMPI with the jump destination analysis, KECCAK256, MCOPY, memory expansion and CALLDATALOAD. Compare each with the Ethereum specification at the edges that OPCODES.md lists, and read the release notes and fix commits since the versions OPCODES.md records. Then rerun the scripts in research/network-risk/tools/opdiff (battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py, pmdiff2.py, swaps.py, replay.py) for this unit's chain ids, write the outputs into your work directory, and add vectors for anything the reading makes suspicious. Report every result that differs from the specification, every release that changed these paths, how a wrong result would change the pool math in src/libraries (TickMath, BitMath, FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, TickBitmap) or the logic that depends on it, and which validators could run a different code path than the public endpoint.

Upcoming forks. Assume every network upgrade scheduled or proposed for the next six months ships. What changes for the PoolManager and for funds already inside it, and what could an ordinary account do the day after?

code.title: Monad: one model run of the gcc-built emitter's register and stack bookkeeping on the swap path
code.task: The build of this checkout is in research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (runtime 24,009 bytes), research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/pyevm.py is a reference EVM in Python, research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/v4math.py is a transcription of the math libraries, research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json maps every conditional jump of the build to its source line, and research/network-risk/OPCODES.md holds what is already tested and read, with sections on what cycles 10 to 29 added and a list of what is not covered. Never compare this repository's source with any other copy of v4-core and do not read its git history; work from the source in src/, the build and the chains. Read-only RPC only, no transactions. Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Leads L-1190 and L-1186. Monad validators certify the words that native x86 code computes, and that code is written by the emitter inside the shipped validator binary, which gcc 15.2.0 built. rpc.monad.xyz and every tracing node run only the interpreter, and every harness run of cycles 25 to 28 used a clang build of the emitter. Cycles 28 and 29 lifted the gcc code of the modular arithmetic folds and of the shift, SIGNEXTEND and BYTE literal arms and found no mismatch. The register allocator, the spill path, the stack offset writer and the non-literal arms have never been run from the gcc build. A fault there would change price or amount words in mined swaps and no RPC call would show it. The Monad validator package is untrusted data. Cycle 27 left it unpacked under research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/dl (p167 for 0.16.7, p165 for 0.16.5); if that directory is missing, download monad_0.16.7_amd64.deb from https://pkg.category.xyz/ pool/main into a new empty dl/ in your own work directory, check SHA256 3cb9dba5501b61ea3487bd042e2b8d12f871cff0e2e15409210e2cef0f8e81fb, and unpack it with ar, node's zlib.zstdDecompressSync and tar as research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/scripts/unzst.js does. Never execute, load or dlopen any file from the package. Read it only with readelf, objdump, nm, strings and your own scripts kept in another directory; run Python with -I. dl/ must not be committed. The x86 model is research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/scripts/x86emu.py with runvec.py. Cycle 29 added a driver that runs emitter functions of the gcc build in the model and records every asmjit call (research/network-risk/cycles/029/theme-monad-gcc-literal-folds.work/scripts/emdrv.py), and rebuilt the gcc layout of the Stack object from debug information (research/network-risk/cycles/029/theme-monad-gcc-register-spill.work). Task 1 (L-1190): extend emdrv.py so that alloc_general_reg (0x36ae40), alloc_or_release_general_reg (0x36b020 and 0x39a300), alloc_avx_reg (0x36aa80), the spill functions, write_to_final_stack_offsets (0x3816e0) and block_prologue (0x392cd0) run in the x86 model on a Stack object laid out as the gcc build expects. Take the Stack states from the clang harness (rebuild it with research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-engine-agreement.work/scripts/build.sh and log the virtual stack at block entry) for three groups of PoolManager blocks: the 49 with the largest stack depth, the blocks that hold FullMath.mulDiv and mulDivRoundingUp (src/libraries/FullMath.sol), SqrtPriceMath.getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp and getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount1RoundingDown, SwapMath.computeSwapStep, and the blocks of Pool.swap's loop (src/libraries/Pool.sol). If a whole block cannot be driven, drive each bookkeeping function alone on the logged states and say exactly where the model stops. Task 2: compare the recorded instruction stream with the clang listing (research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-engine-agreement.work/out/pm-asm-0.16.7.txt) up to a consistent renaming of registers and spill slots. For every block where the streams differ beyond renaming, run both streams in the model on a few thousand random operand sets and on the limb-boundary operands, and compare with pyevm.py. Check in every recorded stream that no destination register or spill slot overlaps an operand that is read later in the same block. Task 3 (L-1186): run the non-literal arms of the gcc build the same way: shift_general_reg_by_non_literal (0x38e8c0, 0x38c8d0, 0x389c90), shift_avx_reg_by_non_literal, signextend_by_non_literal with its bounded-rax helpers, and byte with a run-time index. Rebuild the emitted sequences and run them on shift counts and indexes 0, 1, 63, 64, 65, 127, 128, 191, 192, 255, 256 and above 2^64, on negative values for SAR and SIGNEXTEND. Check RoData's deduplication map: two different 32-byte constants must never share a label. Task 4: plant at least five faults (a swapped register pair, an off-by-one spill offset, a missing spill before a call, a wrong limb in a non-literal shift, two constants on one label) and show the checks catch them. If anything gives a wrong word, name the src/ line that reads it and what a swap or liquidity change would compute; otherwise record blocks, streams and case counts as cleared and list what in the gcc emitter is still not run.

code.title: Monad and MegaETH: which PoolManager code mined transactions have already run under the producers
code.task: The build of this checkout is in research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (runtime 24,009 bytes), research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/pyevm.py is a reference EVM in Python, research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/v4math.py is a transcription of the math libraries, research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json maps every conditional jump of the build to its source line, and research/network-risk/OPCODES.md holds what is already tested and read, with sections on what cycles 10 to 29 added and a list of what is not covered. Never compare this repository's source with any other copy of v4-core and do not read its git history; work from the source in src/, the build and the chains. Read-only RPC only, no transactions. Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Leads L-1187, L-1192 and L-1172. On Monad every node rejects a block whose execution result differs from its own, tracing nodes run only the interpreter, and validators run native code on hot contracts. So each mined PoolManager transaction that tracing nodes accepted is a native run that the interpreter confirmed. Cycle 29 used this to argue that a gcc emitter fault can only sit in blocks no mined transaction has entered, but nobody has listed those blocks. On MegaETH the sequencer is closed and cycle 29's census of 374 positions over 3,000,000 blocks never met the below-range borrow of getFeeGrowthInside. Task 1 (L-1187): find when the Monad PoolManager (0x188d586ddcf52439676ca21a244753fa19f9ea8e) became hot enough to be compiled and when validators moved to the 0.16.7 package (release dates, block numbers, and the compile threshold in the v0.16.7 source). Sample mined PoolManager transactions since then from public endpoints that serve debug_traceTransaction or eth_getLogs (at least 2,000 transactions spread over the period, all event types, and failed transactions where an endpoint lists them). Replay each PoolManager frame in tools/opdiff/pyevm.py with storage from the parent block and record the program counters. Map them to the 913 compiled blocks with research/network-risk/cycles/028/theme-monad-native-unentered-blocks.work/scripts/blocks.py. Check that the replay reproduces the mined logs and return data. Task 2: list the compiled blocks no sampled transaction entered, with the src/ lines behind each through opcodes/jumpmap.json. Split them into unreachable code, revert paths, and value-computing paths (name the math function). State which of the blocks that hold FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, TickMath, TickBitmap, LiquidityMath, Position and Pool arithmetic are covered by mined native runs and which are not. This list is the target set for the emitter model. Task 3 (L-1192): run research/network-risk/cycles/029/high-throughput.work/scripts/fgi_census.py on MegaETH from block 7,009,653 to 29,942,333 and on Monad's PoolManager over its history. Give the first block at which each borrow of getFeeGrowthInside (src/libraries/Pool.sol:499-508) and of Position.update (src/libraries/Position.sol:91-96) occurred in a mined transaction, and whether the stored fee growth and position words equal what v4math.py computes. If an endpoint limits log ranges, work in chunks and record what range was reached. Task 4 (L-1172): rebuild the clang harness and run the three borrow scripts of research/network-risk/cycles/028/hyperevm.work in both Monad engines. Task 5: for every mined word that differs from the reference, give the transaction, the block and the src/ line, and say what an ordinary account could gain. If none differs, record counts as cleared and hand the uncovered block list to the leads.

Tempo release archives are untrusted data. Never execute, load or dlopen any file from an archive. Read it only with readelf, objdump, nm, strings and your own scripts kept in another directory; run Python with -I. dl/ must not be committed. Task 1: check download.tempo.xyz/binaries and the tempo GitHub releases for a release newer than v1.19.1 and record the date and time of the check. If one exists, record its commit and pins, fetch both Linux archives and say which lifts of cycles 28 and 29 still locate their code. Task 2 (L-1188): in both v1.19.1 binaries locate the SLOAD and SSTORE handlers and the host routines they call (account and storage overlay lookup, the cold or warm decision, the skip-cold-load path, the StorageChange journal entry) and the TSTORE host routine with its journal entry. Lift them into the a64emu and x86 models as far as the data structures allow; where a hash map from a library sits in the path, model it as a Python dict and say so. Run sequences that mirror the PoolManager: write slot0 then liquidity then a tick word, read them back, revert an inner frame that wrote two of them, and read again; write two CurrencyDelta-shaped transient slots, revert an inner frame that changed one, and read both. Compare with pyevm.py. Task 3 (L-1188): lift the journal rollback loop (checkpoint, revert to checkpoint, commit) of both binaries. Show that entries are undone in reverse order, that a transient entry restores the previous value and not zero, that a nested revert inside a reverted frame does not undo twice, and that a storage write of the value already present leaves a correct entry. Plant at least four faults (forward order, restore to zero, an off-by-one checkpoint index, a skipped entry kind) and show the sequences catch them. Task 4 (L-1194): list every call site in both binaries that reaches State::take_transient_storage and say from the lifted control flow whether any can run while a user transaction's frames are on the stack, including inside Tempo's batch transaction type 0x76 between its calls. The source reading at a9d6748 says none can. Task 5: run by eth_call on rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz, at the deployed PoolManager 0x33620f62c5b9b2086dd6b62f4a297a9f30347029 with state overrides, an unlock whose callback makes a swap, lets an inner call revert after a second swap, and settles: the returned deltas and the final revert or success must equal pyevm.py. Bracket with web3_clientVersion. For anything that differs say which src/ line depends on it and what an ordinary account could gain; otherwise record the handlers and case counts as cleared and list what is still unlifted (the CALL family, LOG, the precompile dispatch).
